title: Feature slab switchback: headcount velocity vs unit price probe
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet experiments with a 'slab switchback' play: dynamically shifting committed capacity (slab) to on-demand/spot (spot) for specific feature surface areas as unit price and token demand move. Goal: identify headcount (HC) velocity and short-term contractor substitution needed to keep SLAs while protecting gross margin if unit price compresses (or recovers).

Key takeaways (high level):
- A 12% sustained unit-price compression (per-token) vs base requires ~9% reduction in upstream inference HC (ops/infra) and ~3 FTE replacement with contractors to maintain runbooks for burst capacity.
- Short-duration price rebounds (>=8% in 6–8 weeks) favor a fast re-commit to slab for high-throughput features; this requires a 3-week ops playbook and 1.5 FTE of rampable SRE/infra time.
- Mixed GPU-mix (A100->H100 substitution) reduces per-token cost by ~6% but increases HC skill premium by ~18% for short-term hiring/contractors.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline monthly token volume (all features): 9.6B tokens.
- Feature split for experiment: Search assist (40%), Conversational UI (35%), Back-office rerank (25%).
- Baseline unit price: $0.0009 per token effective internal cost (weighted GPU+infra amortized).
- Slab commitment discount: 22% vs on-demand spot price at baseline utilization (70% realized).
- Contractor blended loaded rate: $120/hr; Full-time equivalent (FTE) blended fully-burdened annual comp: $240k.
- Time to hire (FTE): 10–12 weeks; contractor ramp: 1–3 weeks.

Simple scenario outputs (monthly, rounded):
CSV table (role, baseline-FTE, conservative-FTE, aggressive-FTE):
infra-engineering, 18, 16, 20
platform-sre, 9, 8, 11
model-ops, 6, 5, 7
cost-accounting/finance-ops, 3, 3, 3
contractor-equivalents (short-term), 0, 2, 0

Price sensitivity scenarios (multi-month view):
1) Baseline (0% price change): Maintain slab for Search assist and Conversational UI; 70% utilization, committed cost per token = $0.000702 (after slab discount).
2) Price compression -12% sustained: Demand elasticity modeled as -0.35 (conservative). Effective token volume falls 4.2% but cost per token (spot) remains and margin shrinks. Operational impacts: reduce slab on rerank feature first, move 40% of rerank to spot; reallocate infra FTEs: -2 infra-engineering FTE, +2 contractor-weeks for migration automation.
3) Price rebound +10% (short spike 6 weeks): Maintain spot for rerank, pre-warm slab for Search assist. Requires +1.5 FTE infra SRE burn for 3 weeks to re-commit and validate.

Projected P&L delta table (monthly delta vs baseline, values in $k):
Scenario, gross-token-cost-delta, headcount-cost-delta, net-delta
Price -12%,  -18.4, +12.5, -5.9
Price +10% (spike), +9.6, +8.1, +17.7
Slab->spot shift (partial), -6.2, -4.8, -11.0

Operational runbook (short checklist):
- Trigger: 7-day rolling unit-price move > |6%| or token velocity > |10%| growth/decay.
- Phase A (detect, 0–7d): finance-run quick-scan, flag impacted SKU routes, message GTM/customer-SRE owners.
- Phase B (execute, 7–28d): reconfigure slab scaling rules on rerank routes, start contractor automation sprint (2 people, 3 weeks).
- Phase C (stabilize, 28–90d): observe utilization; either re-commit slab (if price rebound) or capacity-tilt to spot (if compression persists).

Detailed monthly headcount plan (quarterly roll):
- Q1 (plan): hire 1 infra-engineer, maintain SRE, freeze model-ops hiring.
- Q2 (stress): delay 1 infra-engineer hire if price compression persists; shift 30% of rerank traffic to spot and onboard 2 contractors for migration work.
- Q3 (rebound): accelerate slab re-commit if utilization >75% on Search assist for 4 consecutive weeks; convert top contractor to FTE if velocity sustained.

Sensitivity waterfall (how to interpret):
- Input lever: unit price change (±%); secondary lever: token elasticity (0 to -0.8); tertiary: slab utilization delta (±20 pts).
- Output metric: required HC delta (FTEs) to keep 95th percentile latency SLO and throughput.

Scratch calculations (not exhaustive)  — monthly numbers in $k: 
- Baseline token cost = 9.6B * $0.0009 = $8,640k (~$8.64M per month). NOTE: This is intentionally high to stress-test pricing (internal-only projection).
- If slab discount realized: effective monthly cost = $8,640k * (1 - 0.22) = $6,739k.
- Price -12% scenario token cost if shifted 25% to spot = (0.75*9.6B*0.000792) + (0.25*9.6B*0.0009*0.88) = (calculation rough) ~ $6,800k (rounded).

Risks & open questions:
- Customer churn risk if latency/availability degrades during slab->spot migrations; need KT and canary-ing with top 10 customers.
- Contract law: can we break slab commit mid-quarter without penalty? Need legal confirmation on commit clauses and re-commit windows.
- Forecast sensitivity: our elasticity guess (-0.35) is weakly validated; product telemetry A/B should run to measure actual response before large staffing moves.

Recommended next steps (immediate, 0–30d):
1) Finance + Product run two quick A/B telemetry experiments (Search assist and Rerank) to capture demand elasticity over 4 weeks.
2) Legal to review slab break clauses and identify re-commit windows.
3) Ops to prepare a 3-week contractor onboarding template (SRE + infra automation) and a 1-week canary script for feature migration.
4) Build a small automated dashboard (token price vs utilization vs slab-commit-cost) for daily monitoring; owners: Finance (Priya), Platform (Ethan).

Appendix (links to internal tools & quick refs):
- Price/usage dashboard: /internal/dashboards/price-velocity (placeholder)
- Jira for procurement/commit changes: JIRA-FIN-7823
- Playbook prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/price-sim-proto

Notes to reviewers: this is a working experiment; numbers are intentionally approximate and purposefully conservative on elasticity. Looking for: legal on commit flexibility, ops on contractor ramp feasibility, and product on telemetry instrumentation priority.
